leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight round-1 configurations place the optical lattice clock alone, to Katori and Ye. All six cite the magic-wavelength concept (Katori) and the 10^-18 demonstration and many-body clock work (Ye), reproduction at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST, and downstream reach into tests of constants, dark-sector couplings, relativistic geodesy and the redefinition of the second. The citations differ in emphasis: some centre on invention plus precision realisation, others on development to the 10^-18 level, and Lindroth's adds fundamental-physics tests and the measurement of time. Every supporter also records the same reservations: adjacency to the 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (ion control) prizes, whether this is metrology rather than discovery, and that the redefinition of the second is still pending. Several supporters moved to this configuration after reading the other ballots (Danielsson from B035, Olsson from B050, Johansson from circuit QED), so the support is a post-reading convergence and not six independent first choices. Two of the six (Kroll, Lindroth) described a more specific citation as a safeguard against the novelty objection.

Eriksson alone keeps time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as the single prize part. The argument is a new state of matter with a symmetry-based invariant, an experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, and confirmation across many materials over roughly twenty years. Eriksson concedes that attribution is fragile (the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal of HgTe, the 3D topological insulator work, and the 2016 topological-phases prize) and names B013 as the safer fallback. B048 appears as an explicit alternative for Johansson and Mehlig, but not as a preferred configuration for anyone else.

Mehlig alone prefers the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase (Berry, Aharonov) as a unifying conceptual root for the Chern-number, quantum Hall and topological-band programmes. Mehlig states that it is the weakest candidate on opening support and that priority (Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam, Mead-Truhlar, Herzberg-Longuet-Higgins, Simon), the deceased Bohm, and age are real obstacles; B048 and B013 are the stated fallbacks. Lindroth lists B034 as a third alternative but prefers B013.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members explicitly name Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye as the proposed laureates for B013 in their opening ballots, and six of eight prefer B013 as the whole prize in round 1. Eriksson and Mehlig both name B013 as a fallback.
Reproducibility across independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) is cited by every B013 supporter as the reason the 10^-18 result can be trusted.

Every B013 supporter and the two dissenters who mention it flag the same three vulnerabilities: adjacency to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, the metrology-versus-discovery question, and the pending redefinition of the second.

B001 is a recurring second-tier candidate: it is listed as an alternative by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson and Pearce, and where laureates were named by the members who support it (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger) the experimental trio recurs. It is not preferred by any member in round 1.
Members who favour condensed-matter candidates (B048, B041, B034) explicitly accept that credit or timing problems make them harder than B013 and name B013 or B048 as fallbacks.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a discovery or a technique: Danielsson, Johansson and Lindroth describe it as metrology or refinement even while preferring it, and no fundamental-physics result (varying constants, dark-sector signal) has yet come out of the clocks. Pearce, Kroll and Olsson answer that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct invention with a clear mechanism.

Whether the committee should reward a new state of matter (Eriksson, B048) or a unifying conceptual root (Mehlig, B034) instead of a measurement capability (B013). Mehlig notes that several candidates are downstream applications of the geometric-phase idea.

How far B013 is separable from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes: Kroll argues that the many-atom statistical gain is something ion clocks cannot offer, whereas Olsson notes that an optical comb is a necessary technical foundation for any optical clock.

Whether the IceCube result (B035) and the circuit-QED candidate (B008) are mature enough: B035 source identification still rests on a few objects, and Johansson has explicitly withdrawn circuit QED as his own top choice.
attribution_disputes: B013: Katori and Ye are named by all eight, but Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson note that Ludlow, Lemke, Hinkley, Bloom, Takamoto, Lemonde, Campbell and Hollberg did much of the concept-adjacent or hands-on work, and Lindroth says she cannot weigh these contributions reliably. Pearce and Olsson both flag the ytterbium and Al+ lineages as adjacent.

B048: Eriksson states that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal was decisive and that Zhang's death means it cannot be repaired by adding him, and that the 3D topological insulator work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Roy, Hsieh-Hasan) cannot be covered by a three-person cap.

B034: Mehlig names the contested priority (Ehrenberg-Siday 1949, Pancharatnam, Mead-Truhlar, Herzberg-Longuet-Higgins, Simon) and that Bohm is deceased, so the 1959 effect could be recognised only through Aharonov.
B035: Pearce notes that naming Halzen and Spiering would leave out the DUMAND and AMANDA lineage and the collaboration leadership.

B001: the opening laureate lists differ (Johansson and Lindroth name Zoller instead of Esslinger; the other supporters name Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger), and Cirac is on the ballot's credited names but on no member's proposed list.
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the redefinition of the second before recognising B013: Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all list this as a reservation. Kroll and Pearce argue that the prize recognises demonstrated performance, not the metrological decision.
Whether B034 is too old or reads as an afterthought after the 2016 topological-phases prize and the quantum Hall prizes (Mehlig).
Whether B035 should wait for firmer source catalogues (Pearce, Danielsson) and whether B048 is mature enough given a roughly twenty-year-stable interpretation but unresolved credit (Eriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce, as Chair, discloses that his own background is in astroparticle physics and instrumentation, not in atomic or condensed-matter physics, and that he relies on colleagues and expert reviewers for B013 priority. No member discloses a personal or institutional conflict or requests recusal in the round-1 files.
Lindroth and Olsson each state that they recall priority from memory and not from verified documents and cannot reliably weigh some lattice-clock contributions.
questions_for_round2: For B013, what exactly distinguishes the lattice-clock contribution from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and can a citation be written around magic-wavelength trapping and the 10^-18 many-atom realisation without implying a third clock prize?

Is the two-name Katori and Ye attribution defensible against the roles of Ludlow, Lemke, Hinkley, Bloom, Takamoto, Lemonde and the ion-clock lineage, and is an expert review of the earlier lattice-clock proposals needed before a final ballot?

Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second, and if not, which criterion for a delivered fundamental-physics result (a varying constant, a dark-sector limit, a geodesy measurement) would the B013 supporters count as sufficient?

Can Eriksson state a three-person B048 citation that survives the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D topological insulator objections, and can Mehlig state a B034 priority statement that survives the Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam and Bohm questions? If not, will they move to B013 or another fallback?

If B013 is not the whole prize, does any member want to add a second part, and which of B001 (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger versus Zoller), B035 or B041 would they support, given that none is preferred by any member in round 1?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 files, B013 is the single configuration preferred by a majority (six of eight), with one member each for B048 and B034 who both name B013 as a fallback. The dispute concerns novelty against earlier clock-related prizes, the breadth of credit beyond two names, and timing relative to the redefinition of the second. Several B013 supporters moved to it after reading the other ballots, so round 2 should test the reasons for that convergence and not only its size. As Chair I record that I am in the B013 group and that I am not a specialist in atomic physics.
